title: BALL
operator: SCION 059 · Ball — Graphic Constancy Across Sources

score.note: newly composed synthetic taps; no source audio used

events.label: sun through cloud. The opening anchor. A sun behind cloud is the plainest circle in the archive, bright enough to set the target size and centre. Held 3.5 s so the viewer learns where the rim lives before anything changes.
the Earth, painted globe. A painted globe from a climate film. The first change of kind: from a sky object to a model of one. The rim lands within 5 px of the sun's.

a lens over the moon map. First of three lenses (moon map, signature, eye), from two films twenty years apart. The archive keeps showing someone looking through a circle. Chosen because the use changes while the pose stays the same.
a lens over a signature. Second lens, over a handwritten signature. The rim is the lens's own metal ring, so it registers within 4 px.
a lens over an eye. Third lens: the circle looks back. An eye behind glass, in the same place on screen as the sun was.

a wall clock. A wall clock from a 1966 earthquake film: the first circle that measures something. The second hand keeps moving inside the held rim. The source clip is 720×480, so the anchor is about 22 px off.
a slide-rule dial, BORON. A slide-rule dial. A second measuring circle; its twin on the right is cut by the crop. Rim error under 3 px.

an octagonal clock: the rim fails. The irregular object. An octagonal clock whose edge is not a circle. The anchor was set by hand and left approximate (rim about 29 px small), so the registration visibly fails here instead of being corrected.

RELEASE: a hand at the gauge panel. The contextual release. Unregistered and whole frame, with the expected beat withheld. A hand turns a control beside the gauge panel: the first shot in which a circle is used rather than shown.
a shower rose. After the instruments, the bathroom. A shower head from a 1956 appliance film, rim within 3 px. The taps return here, slower.
a speaker grille and a pointer. A speaker grille and a pointer from a 1929 cartoon. A paper-surfaced circle that looks like a dial and turns out to be a voice.

a film reel in a boy's hands. A film reel in a boy's hands: the archive's own medium turns up as a circle. The tilted ellipse and the boy's movement make the registration drift about 25 px, kept as an honest seam. It stands in for the prompt's object used in play.

a motorcycle wheel, running. A motorcycle wheel. The rim was marked by hand on gridded frames because the detector kept reading the hub. The wheel moves, so it drifts: the first circle that goes somewhere.
a jet intake. A jet intake, 2007: the last registered circle and the largest dark disc. It ends at 35.2 s, before the source clip's own page-turn transition.

EXIT: a painted moon drifts out of frame. The exit. Unregistered. In a 1965 space-animation clip a painted moon drifts out to the left and leaves the starfield empty, then the image fades. The circle leaves the frame in a moving shot, as the prompt asks.
